title: ‘We Have to Take Over’: Far-Right Extremists Want to Seize Control of the GOP
gist: After a Democratic midterm sweep, white-nationalist, Christian-nationalist and Proud Boys figures are declaring MAGA dead and calling for a 'hostile takeover' of the GOP, betting on a backlash; IREHR data show 71% of called races with far-right-Facebook-linked candidates were still won, and far-right ballot measures passed in several states.

themes.theme: Far-right bid to capture the GOP

insights.claim: Following the Democrats' midterm sweep, white nationalist Nick Fuentes publicly called for his 'Groyper' followers to take over the Republican Party, warning GOP leadership it must cooperate or face further sabotage.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Signals intensifying intra-right factional conflict that could raise GOP primary volatility ahead of 2028.

themes.theme: Electoral footprint despite the Democratic sweep

insights.claim: IREHR tracked 535 statewide-race candidates who were members of at least one far-right Facebook group; of 476 called races, 338 won—a 71% win rate, mostly GOP incumbents retaining seats.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Far-right-linked officeholders remain entrenched at the state level even in a Democratic wave year.
insights.locator: The Institute for Research and Education

insights.claim: Even where far-right-aligned candidates lost, they still captured 41–47% of the vote, which IREHR's research director reads as evidence of a sizable mobilizable base.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: A large residual base sustains incentives for extremist mobilization regardless of headline election outcomes.
insights.quote: even in those places where they lost, they're getting 41-47 percent of the vote, [so] there's still a mass base to try to be mobilized,”

insights.claim: Arizona, Colorado, Nebraska and Washington voters approved bans on trans athletes in female sports, and states also passed voter-ID and anti-immigrant ballot measures, which extremist groups cited as proof voters want what the GOP failed to deliver.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Ballot measures are decoupling policy outcomes from party control, a channel investors should watch for state-level regulatory shifts.
